$comment: NEW FILE. CLAUDE.md rules 6 and 9 exist only as English sentences, but SPEC section 5 asks CI to enforce both mechanically. This file is the machine-readable form. Changing it is an editorial act, not a refactor.

field_names.$comment: Rule 9 — no personal data beyond public role. These are matched against every OBJECT KEY appearing anywhere under /data, at any depth, case-insensitively, after stripping non-alphanumerics. A match fails the build outright. Note that Form 26 affidavits do print a candidate's father's name, spouse's assets, and address: the rule is that we do not extract them, so the field must never exist in the first place.
field_names.note: 'category' is included because Indian official forms use it as a euphemism for caste category (SC/ST/OBC/General). If a legitimate non-caste use for that key ever appears, rename the key rather than weakening this list.

vocabulary.$comment: Rule 6 — neutral vocabulary only. SCOPE MATTERS: rule 6 bans these in 'generated content, label, or alt text'. It does NOT reach verbatim source material, because an affidavit that says 'accused' says 'accused' and paraphrasing a source to dodge a wordlist would be a worse failure than the word itself. So the check runs on generated and editorial strings and skips fields that hold source text verbatim.

criminal.note: Rule 6 bans 'criminal' only as an adjective for a person. Legal usage is unavoidable and correct.

checked_fields.$comment: Dotted paths, checked against generated and editorial strings under /data.

exempt_fields.$comment: Verbatim source material or structural pointers into a document. Never rewritten to satisfy a wordlist.

also_checked.$comment: Outside /data: every label rendered by the interface. predicates.json labels are checked because rule 6 says to use them verbatim, so a bad label would propagate everywhere. Site source files are checked once /site exists.

placeholder_data.$comment: Both supplied example files say 'never publish sample data', but nothing stopped it: the sample source's sha256 is 64 zeros, which satisfies the ^[a-f0-9]{64}$ pattern and passes the 'a source lacks sha256' gate. These patterns fail the build if they appear anywhere under /data.
placeholder_data.sha256_denylist_note: The second is the SHA-256 of the empty string — a real hash of nothing at all.
